issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch for Animal and its concrete subclasses (Seal, Pig, Goat): the problem UML and the template Main instantiate animals with a single String parameter (name) and the UML lists only a 'name' attribute, while the solution's Animal.java and subclasses declare a second 'age' attribute and provide constructors taking (String name, int age). This means code examples in the template Main (e.g. Seal("Clarabelle")) and the UML/spec expect single-arg constructors but the solution requires two arguments, which will confuse students and can cause compilation errors or prevent them from following the provided Main usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Make constructors consistent across artifacts. Options: (A) Remove the extra 'age' attribute from the solution and change the Animal and subclass constructors to a single-argument form Animal(String name) / Seal(String name) / Pig(String name) / Goat(String name) to match the UML and template Main; or (B) keep the age attribute but update the problem statement (UML) and template Main to require and demonstrate two-argument constructors (String name, int age). As a minimal compatibility fix, add single-argument constructors in the solution that delegate to the existing two-argument constructors (e.g., Seal(String name) { this(name, 0); }) so the provided Main examples compile while preserving the added age field.
